input.quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale: Section 7.2 (the first clause numbered 7.2) conditions our ability to engage any other provider on first disclosing a competing offer and giving Vendor the chance to match it — a de facto exclusivity/right of first refusal binding Customer for the whole term, with no defined product category, no 12-month limit and no exit on Vendor's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates. It therefore fails the fallback and sits in walk-away territory. Flipping the mandatory operator so that Customer is not required to disclose or match delivers the preferred position (no exclusivity and no sole-supplier obligation on Customer) with the smallest operative change, and removes the conflict with Section 12.3. Exclusivity running in our favour is untouched.

ops.oldText: must disclose and match for Vendor
ops.newText: is not required to disclose or match for Vendor

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have flipped the disclose-and-match operator so that engaging another provider is not conditioned on giving Cobalt a chance to match: as drafted it is an open-ended right of first refusal and de facto exclusivity on us, and our position is no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Customer. It also contradicts Section 12.3, in which Cobalt acknowledges we have given no exclusivity or most-favoured-customer commitment.
proposal.summary: Turn Section 7.2 disclose-and-match obligation into an express no-obligation, removing the de facto exclusivity/ROFR on Customer.
